character._note: ownerRef now carries its canonical `$ref: "player"` (ADR-062 rule 7) AND `visible: false` + `readOnly: true`. Both halves are load-bearing and the second is why the first is finally safe. HISTORY: ef7346c dropped the $ref because adding it alone BROKE the character create dialog — `character.ocName` already declares `$ref: "player"`, and a second player-targeted relation made tests/e2e/spec-coverage/detail-forms-admin.spec.ts `character create dialog exposes a player (ocName) selector` fail on `input[placeholder*="player" i]` (1 failed / 170 passed, two independent runs on PR #289). That measurement stands — for THAT arm. It does not apply here, because nc-vue's `fieldsFromSchema()` drops `visible: false` (and readOnly) properties as its FIRST filter, before any `$ref` is read or any selector is resolved (nextcloud-vue src/utils/schema.js). A hidden property therefore cannot contribute a second player selector to the dialog. The visibility is also correct on its own merits and NOT a gate dodge: `ownerRef` is the portal-subject scoping key, stamped server-side by PortalObjectWriter and excluded from the player projection — it was never meant to be typed by a user, and its direct sibling `ownerUid` has carried `visible: false` + `readOnly: true` in larpingapp_register.json all along. This aligns ownerRef with ownerUid. See ConductionNL/.github#231.

ownerRef.title: Owner
ownerRef.description: UUID reference to the player object — the portal-subject scoping key; distinct from ownerUid which is the Nextcloud user id
